system_overview: This specification models a fair solution to the readers-writers problem, a classic concurrency challenge where multiple processes compete for access to a shared resource. Some processes wish to read (and can do so concurrently with other readers) while others wish to write (requiring exclusive access). This solution uses a first-come-first-served queue to prevent starvation of either readers or writers, ensuring fair access to the shared resource.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a fixed number of actor processes, each of which can request either read or write access to a shared resource. A waiting queue maintains the order in which access requests arrive. Actors transition between four states: idle, waiting in the queue, actively reading or writing, and stopping their activity.
state_variables: The system tracks three pieces of state: (1) the set of processes currently reading the shared resource, (2) the set of processes currently writing to the shared resource, and (3) an ordered queue of pending access requests, where each request records whether the process wants to read or write and which process made the request.
initial_state: No process is reading. No process is writing. The waiting queue is empty.
actions: Processes can perform five types of actions: (1) Request to read: a process that is not already waiting to read joins the end of the waiting queue with a read request. (2) Request to write: a process that is not already waiting to write joins the end of the waiting queue with a write request. (3) Begin reading or writing: if the queue is non-empty and no process is currently writing, the request at the front of the queue is examined. If it is a read request, the process begins reading. If it is a write request and no process is currently reading, the process begins writing. In both cases, the request is removed from the front of the queue. (4) Stop activity: any process that is currently reading or writing may voluntarily stop, removing itself from the active reader or writer set.
safety_properties: Two safety conditions are maintained: (1) Readers and writers are never simultaneously active -- if any process is writing, no process is reading, and vice versa. (2) At most one writer is active at any time.
liveness_properties: Every process eventually gets to read and eventually gets to write. Every active reader eventually stops reading and every active writer eventually stops writing. These properties together ensure no process is starved of access.
model_bounds: The number of actor processes is declared as a constant. For model checking, this must be instantiated with a specific finite value.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on all actions: requesting to read, requesting to write, processing the queue, and stopping activity. This ensures that every enabled action eventually occurs, preventing indefinite postponement. The queue-based design provides first-come-first-served fairness, distinguishing this solution from simpler readers-preference or writers-preference approaches that can cause starvation.
